notes: The RGB themes pulse again — and this time they cannot stop. The hue cycle was driven by requestAnimationFrame, which a phone is free to stop handing over: a WebView that is on screen but not composing frames (after the screen went off, a call, a lifecycle transition, or under memory pressure) gets no frames at all while its timers keep running. The accents then stayed frozen on the hue of the last frame that did run — the RGB theme’s own pink, stuck, exactly like the plain pink theme with nothing pulsing. The cycle runs on a timer now, so it keeps moving whenever the app is on screen, and every tick works the hue out from the clock rather than from an increment — so a timer the system suspended comes back on the right colour instead of carrying on from a stale one

Coming back to the app re-arms the cycle. The phone can shut timers down while the app is away (and Android hands a backgrounded page almost no frames at all), so returning now rebuilds the cycle on the spot instead of trusting whatever was left running. The hue is kept where it was, so nothing snaps back to pink when you reopen the app

A saved cycle speed that cannot work no longer freezes the colour. A stored 0, negative or non-number in the glow-speed setting made every hue a NaN, and CSS ignores an invalid colour — so the accents silently kept the theme’s static colour with no error anywhere. The speed is checked and falls back to eight seconds

Frame one is applied immediately, so even a WebView that never renders a frame shows the theme you picked rather than the previous theme’s accent. The cycle also stops doing anything at all while the app is in the background, which is a little less work for the battery than an animation frame loop that keeps waking the display pipeline
